description: Monitoring Forest Disturbances Aids Management Decisions is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NASA, National Aeronautics and Space Administration; NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information; Oak Ridge National Laboratory. The combined effects of drought, beetle kill, and wildfire are transforming forests in southwestern Colorado. Using satellite data products to monitor the region helps forest caretakers identify vulnerable locations. Coverage: Colorado (2014). The toolkit gives Colorado as the location, 2014 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Since 2004, southwestern Colorado’s Engelmann spruce forests have experienced a severe outbreak of spruce beetles. Episodic outbreaks of spruce beetles have occured multiple times per century, and recent research indicates that they are related to multi-year drought.
